content.title: About
content.content: Egg salad with light mayonnaise is a classic dish that first appeared in 1956. It is made from hard‑boiled eggs, light mayonnaise, mustard, herbs and seasonings. The light mayo contains less fat than traditional versions, keeping the creamy texture while being more diet‑friendly.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The 1956 recipe became popular in post‑war America as people looked for lighter versions of traditional foods.
The original light mayonnaise was made with egg whites and a 1:1 ratio of vegetable oil, reducing calories.
The salad is often used as a sandwich filling, a side for vegetables, or part of a cold buffet.
In the 1970s many variations appeared, adding avocado, yogurt or sour cream.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Eggs provide a complete source of protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs contain B12, riboflavin and folate, which support nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Using light mayonnaise reduces the overall calorie and fat content compared with regular mayo.

items.title: Source of minerals
items.content: The salad supplies iron, phosphorus and selenium, important for blood health and antioxidant protection.

items.title: Satiety support
items.content: The combination of protein and a modest amount of fat helps keep you feeling full longer.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to eggs, ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Eggs contain cholesterol; people with high cholesterol should monitor portion size.

items.title: Mayonnaise shelf life
items.content: Light mayonnaise can spoil quickly if not stored properly, leading to foodborne illness.

items.title: Sodium levels
items.content: Prepared salad can be salty; those watching sodium intake should adjust added salt accordingly.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the egg salad chilled. It can be spread on bread, used as a sandwich filling, tossed with leafy greens, or presented as an appetizer on party platters.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared salad in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Over time the flavor and texture may change, so it is best made in portions.
